title: HA Soundbar Settings
summary: Expose selected advanced Samsung soundbar settings as native Home Assistant entities. It reuses the official SmartThings integration’s connection instead of requiring another saved token. Developed against the HW-Q990F, it complements ordinary media-player controls rather than replacing the soundbar’s whole interface.
features: Bass/subwoofer, centre and rear levels: integer sliders from −6 to +6.
Standard, Surround, Game Pro and Adaptive Sound.
Bass boost, night mode and voice amplifier.
Use the already configured HA SmartThings OAuth session.
Validate and send one setting per command; no automatic write retry.
Show unknown initially and retain the last accepted setting; this is not physical readback.
workflows: First confirm the soundbar already appears in the official SmartThings integration in HA.
Add Mungoon Soundbar Settings, choose the detected soundbar, and open its entities in Devices & services.
Add the relevant number, switch and select entities to a dashboard or use their entity controls directly. The integration itself does not provide a separate custom dashboard.
Choose one control to test, such as Center speaker level. Note your current physical setting independently if you will want to revert.
Move the slider by one whole-number step and listen for the response. Use Voice amplifier only if that is the intended effect.
Avoid changing several controls at once while diagnosing compatibility. A cloud response saying COMPLETED means the request was accepted, not that the setting was measured on the hardware.
Use HA’s normal automation editor and select the Night mode entity. Add the intended on/off action at your chosen trigger.
Optionally set Sound mode using the exact available option labels. Keep this separate from power/volume actions on the ordinary media player.
Test once while you can hear the soundbar. Since writes are not automatically retried, inspect HA errors before repeating a failed command.
Unknown after installation does not mean the soundbar is disconnected: the tested device does not provide advanced-setting readback.
A value shown after an accepted command is the component’s remembered value. A later change on the remote or Samsung app can leave it out of date.
Use the physical device to confirm actual state when it matters. Full graphic equalizer bands are not provided by this component.
limits: Only the supported command payloads are promised. Other Samsung models require testing. Three command tests passed previously; no sound settings or physical-device tests were changed during this documentation work.
